main.title: Sega GT 2002
main.subtitle: A racing career begins with an affordable car
main.summary: Sega GT 2002 is Wow Entertainment's Xbox racing simulation, released in North America on 3 September 2002. The player begins a career with a limited budget, buys a car and enters events to earn the money needed for improvements or another vehicle. Timed licence laps provide milestones without splitting driving into a long sequence of separate manoeuvre tests. The game connects the immediate lap to a developing garage, making each race useful as both a driving challenge and an opportunity to prepare the vehicle that will enter the next event.

cards.heading: A racing career begins with an affordable car
cards.text: Sega GT 2002 is Wow Entertainment's Xbox racing simulation, released in North America on 3 September 2002. The player begins a career with a limited budget, buys a car and enters events to earn the money needed for improvements or another vehicle. Timed licence laps provide milestones without splitting driving into a long sequence of separate manoeuvre tests. The game connects the immediate lap to a developing garage, making each race useful as both a driving challenge and an opportunity to prepare the vehicle that will enter the next event.

cards.heading: Clean driving has a financial consequence
cards.text: A damage meter records contact during a race, reducing the prize money when the car has been knocked around. Finishing without damage can instead produce a cash bonus. Although the damage does not change handling, it affects the career beyond the finishing position, giving the player another reason to avoid an untidy pass. Chronicle Mode offers a different progression through historic cars from the 1960s and early 1970s. Improving those machines and racing newer opposition connects the development of a single car to the broader changes represented by the collection.

cards.heading: Sega's racing series finds a new console home
cards.text: The sequel followed the Dreamcast's Sega GT and later reached many Xbox owners through a bundled disc shared with Jet Set Radio Future. Quick Battle, Time Attack and replay tools offered alternatives to the career, while Sega GT Online subsequently expanded the concept with additional cars and network play. Reviews were generally favourable. Sega GT 2002 belongs to the period when Sega's console franchises were establishing themselves on other manufacturers' hardware, carrying a recognisable garage-building racing structure into an Xbox catalogue increasingly associated with driving games of its own.

main.title: Battlefield 1942
main.summary: Battlefield 1942 is a 2002 first-person shooter game developed by Digital Illusions CE and published by Electronic Arts for Microsoft Windows and Mac OS X.

cards.text: Battlefield 1942 is a 2002 first-person shooter game developed by Digital Illusions CE and published by Electronic Arts for Microsoft Windows and Mac OS X. It is the first installment in the Battlefield series. The game can be played in single-player mode against the video game AI or in multiplayer mode against players on the Internet or in a local area network. It is a popular platform for mod developers, with many released modifications that alter the gameplay and theme.

In-game, players assume the role of one of five classes of infantry: Scout, Assault, Anti-Tank, Medic, and Engineer. Players also have the ability to fly various World War II fighter aircraft and bombers, navigate capital ships, submarines, and aircraft carriers, man coastal artillery defenses, drive tanks, APCs and jeeps, and take control of anti-aircraft guns and mounted machine guns.

Each battle takes place on one of several maps located in a variety of places and famous battlefields in all of the major theaters of World War II: the Pacific, European, North African, Eastern, and Italian Fronts. Combat is between the Axis powers and the Allies. The location determines which nation-specific armies are used (for example, on the Wake Island map, it is Japan versus the United States, while on the El Alamein map, it is Germany versus the United Kingdom). The maps in Battlefield 1942 are based on real battles and are somewhat realistically portrayed.

Upon release, Battlefield 1942 received generally favorable reviews, with particular praise directed towards the innovative gameplay, multiplayer, and World War II theme. The game went on to perform well commercially, with over 3 million copies sold by 2004. Since its release, the game has spawned numerous sequels and spin-offs, which ultimately turned into the Battlefield series. Battlefield 1942 is retrospectively considered to be one of the best video games of all time.

main.title: Steel Battalion
main.subtitle: Sit down inside the machine
main.summary: Steel Battalion is a combat simulation released for Xbox in Japan on 12 September 2002. The player pilots a Vertical Tank, a heavily armed walking machine, through missions viewed from its cockpit. Its extraordinary controller is part of the game: two sticks, a throttle, switches, pedals and an eject button spread the controls across the player's desk. Rather than condensing the machine into a few familiar inputs, Nude Maker and Capcom made operating it the central activity. Learning where to reach becomes part of learning how to survive.

cards.heading: Sit down inside the machine
cards.text: Steel Battalion is a combat simulation released for Xbox in Japan on 12 September 2002. The player pilots a Vertical Tank, a heavily armed walking machine, through missions viewed from its cockpit. Its extraordinary controller is part of the game: two sticks, a throttle, switches, pedals and an eject button spread the controls across the player's desk. Rather than condensing the machine into a few familiar inputs, Nude Maker and Capcom made operating it the central activity. Learning where to reach becomes part of learning how to survive.

cards.heading: Start the engine before the battle
cards.text: Each mission begins with a startup procedure. The player brings the tank's systems online before taking it into combat, then manages movement, weapons and the view through its windows. Turning too sharply can topple the machine, while overheating demands another response from the pilot. Even mud on the windscreen has its own control. These details give the cockpit a physical logic: a problem appears in front of the player and a particular switch or action answers it. The controller makes that relationship unusually direct and memorable.

cards.heading: Know when to leave the cockpit
cards.text: The eject button gives defeat a final decision. If the pilot fails to escape a doomed machine, the character dies and the game deletes the save, making another campaign necessary. New generations of Vertical Tank offer different systems and capabilities as progress continues. Hifumi Kono directed the project and Atsushi Inaba produced it, with Naru Shirai composing the music. The expensive controller and limited production restricted its audience, but they also made Steel Battalion a distinctive example of a game built around a purpose-made piece of hardware.

main.title: Quantum Redshift
main.subtitle: A rivalry takes place at racing speed
main.summary: Quantum Redshift is Curly Monsters' futuristic Xbox racing game, released in North America on 17 September 2002. Armed hovercraft race across eight courses, with each driver connected to a particular rival. The player steers a SPARC through the circuit while collecting energy for weapons and protection. Winning means managing the road and the other vehicles at the same time. Alternate routes create choices within the courses, while the tournament's increasing difficulty also increases speed, making a familiar stretch of track demand a more immediate response.

cards.heading: A rivalry takes place at racing speed
cards.text: Quantum Redshift is Curly Monsters' futuristic Xbox racing game, released in North America on 17 September 2002. Armed hovercraft race across eight courses, with each driver connected to a particular rival. The player steers a SPARC through the circuit while collecting energy for weapons and protection. Winning means managing the road and the other vehicles at the same time. Alternate routes create choices within the courses, while the tournament's increasing difficulty also increases speed, making a familiar stretch of track demand a more immediate response.

cards.heading: Choose when to spend the energy collected
cards.text: Colour-coded pickups charge the craft's offensive weapons and shields. Homing and direct-fire attacks provide different ways to interfere with a rival, but staying on the racing line remains essential. Points earned through victories, pickups and defeated opponents can improve the craft between events. Each tournament eventually leads to a Nemesis Challenge against the selected character's rival. The player therefore develops both a vehicle and a relationship with a particular opponent, returning to the track with stronger equipment and a clearer reason to watch one competitor's position.

cards.heading: Wipeout experience meets an Xbox production
cards.text: Curly Monsters included former Psygnosis staff who had worked on Wipeout, including designer Nick Burcombe. Microsoft supported the production with a soundtrack commissioned from Junkie XL and character work involving Satoshi Ueda. Local multiplayer allowed up to four people to race together, while Time Attack let the player pursue a recorded ghost. The game received mixed reviews and did not sell enough to support the planned sequel. Its lasting identity comes from the combination of increasingly fast racing, driver rivalries and a soundtrack written specifically for those high-speed encounters.

main.title: Star Fox Adventures
main.subtitle: Fox leaves the cockpit
main.summary: Star Fox Adventures turned the series towards action-adventure on GameCube in 2002. On Dinosaur Planet, Fox explores interconnected landscapes, solves puzzles and fights with a magical staff; the young dinosaur Tricky assists him with commands. Arwing flights still link parts of the expedition, but exploration on foot sets its rhythm. Nintendo’s original Japanese site dates that release to September 27, while the European edition followed on November 22; the North American launch preceded both on September 23.

cards.heading: A different kind of expedition
cards.text: Star Fox Adventures turned the series towards action-adventure on GameCube in 2002. On Dinosaur Planet, Fox explores interconnected landscapes, solves puzzles and fights with a magical staff; the young dinosaur Tricky assists him with commands. Arwing flights still link parts of the expedition, but exploration on foot sets its rhythm. Nintendo’s original Japanese site dates that release to September 27, while the European edition followed on November 22; the North American launch preceded both on September 23.

cards.heading: The world before the squadron
cards.text: Rare had first developed the project as Dinosaur Planet for Nintendo 64. Composer David Wise later explained that the move to GameCube came before the opportunity to incorporate Star Fox, so references to the series entered the score late in development. That history helps explain its distinctive identity: familiar space-faring characters inhabit a world of temples, forests and dinosaurs, with music built for atmosphere as well as action.

main.title: Sly Cooper and the Thievius Raccoonus
main.summary: Sly Cooper and the Thievius Raccoonus (known as Sly Raccoon in PAL regions) is a 2002 stealth platform video game developed by Sucker Punch Productions and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2.

cards.heading: Sly Cooper and the Thievius Raccoonus
cards.text: Sly Cooper and the Thievius Raccoonus (known as Sly Raccoon in PAL regions) is a 2002 stealth platform video game developed by Sucker Punch Productions and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2. It is the first installment in the Sly Cooper series. The game follows the titular Sly Cooper and his gang, Bentley the Turtle and Murray the Hippo, on their mission to recover the lost pages of the "Thievius Raccoonus" (a book listing every thieving technique created by Sly's ancestors) from a rival gang known as the Fiendish Five.

cards.heading: A hand-drawn look and a continuing series
cards.text: Sly Cooper was praised for its technical achievements—particularly its use of a variation on cel shading to create a film noir feel while still rendering as a hand-drawn animated film—and criticized for being too short. The game was followed by three sequels: Sly 2: Band of Thieves (2004), Sly 3: Honor Among Thieves (2005), and Sly Cooper: Thieves in Time (2013). The first three games were remastered and released as The Sly Collection for the PlayStation 3 and PlayStation Vita on April 16, 2014. Sly Cooper was digitally re-released on PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5 on June 11, 2024.

main.title: Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit 2
main.summary: Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit 2 is a 2002 racing video game, the sixth installment in the Need for Speed series following Porsche Unleashed (2000) and the direct sequel to Need for Speed III: Hot Pursuit (1998).

cards.heading: Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit 2
cards.text: Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit 2 is a 2002 racing video game, the sixth installment in the Need for Speed series following Porsche Unleashed (2000) and the direct sequel to Need for Speed III: Hot Pursuit (1998). It was developed by EA Black Box for the PlayStation 2, and a distinctly different version by EA Seattle for GameCube, Xbox, and Microsoft Windows. Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit 2 features cars from various high-performance and exotic car manufacturers. Players can compete in races using these cars, or opt to play as a police officer and pursue speeders.

cards.heading: Reception and legacy
cards.text: The game features several popular recording artists from its time such as Uncle Kracker, The Humble Brothers and Hot Action Cop. Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit 2 received "generally favorable" reviews on the PS2 and Xbox, while the PC and GameCube versions received "mixed or average" reviews, according to review aggregator platform Metacritic. In 2002, the game was awarded Console Racing Game of the Year at the 6th Annual Interactive Achievement Awards.

main.title: Blinx: The Time Sweeper
main.summary: A sweeper turns loose objects into ammunition while carefully chosen crystals supply powers over time.

cards.heading: Blinx: The Time Sweeper
cards.text: Blinx: The Time Sweeper is Artoon's 2002 Xbox platform adventure, published by Microsoft Game Studios. Its feline cleaner enters a world damaged by stolen time, carrying a machine that sweeps up rubbish and fires it at monsters. Collectible crystals supply another set of tools: the ability to interrupt, reverse or replay what happens around him.

cards.heading: The ammunition is on the floor
cards.text: Blinx fills his sweeper with objects found in the stage, then shoots them back out, starting with the last item collected. A heavy object can deal more damage, but may require a stronger machine to lift. This makes the floor part of the combat system: clear enough space to move, keep something useful loaded and watch which piece will leave the sweeper next. Gold earned during a sweep buys equipment and greater capacity between stages.

cards.heading: Choosing the next few seconds
cards.text: Time powers come from sets of four crystals. Three matching crystals and one other grant a single use; four matching ones grant two. Picking up everything can spoil the combination being assembled. Those choices decide which solution is available at the next obstacle: pause moving machinery, rewind a collapsed structure or record an action and let a copy repeat it. The platforming route depends partly on the powers brought to it, and those powers depend on earlier collecting decisions.

cards.heading: A sweep against the clock
cards.text: Each area allows ten minutes to defeat its time monsters and reach the goal. Moving between platforms is only part of the work: Blinx must locate the remaining enemies, find ammunition and decide when a limited time power is worth spending. Better sweepers also give a reason to return to earlier areas, where heavier objects may conceal another route. The timer gives these small tasks a common pressure, turning an apparently untidy playground into a job that needs a plan.

main.title: TimeSplitters 2
main.summary: TimeSplitters 2 is a first-person shooter video game, developed by Free Radical Design, published by Eidos Interactive, and released in October 2002 for PlayStation 2, Xbox and GameCube.

cards.heading: TimeSplitters 2
cards.text: TimeSplitters 2 is a first-person shooter video game, developed by Free Radical Design, published by Eidos Interactive, and released in October 2002 for PlayStation 2, Xbox and GameCube. The game's story focuses on the efforts of a space marine who seeks to recover powerful time crystals from a race of alien mutants called TimeSplitters, which leads them to taking on the form of an individual dealing with their own problems across different time periods between the 19th and 25th century. The developers focused on expanding the story element following 2000's TimeSplitters, and features influences from various film genres, including horror, action and science fiction.

cards.heading: Cooperation, multiplayer and map-making
cards.text: Alongside the story mode, which can be played solo or co-operatively, players can also engage in multiplayer modes and create their own maps. The game received generally favorable reviews from critics, who praised its improvements on its predecessor as well as its multiplayer gameplay and graphics, though criticised its story and lack of online gameplay. TimeSplitters 2 was later followed by a sequel, TimeSplitters: Future Perfect, in 2005.

cards.heading: The trilogy returns as PS2 Classics
cards.text: TimeSplitters 2, along with the other games in the trilogy, were re-released on the PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5 as a PS2 Classic in 2024, with trophy support, a rewind feature and improved loading times.

main.title: The King of Fighters 2002
main.subtitle: Three fighters return to the foreground
main.summary: The King of Fighters 2002 is Eolith's team fighting game, first released for Neo Geo on 10 October 2002 and published by Playmore.

cards.heading: Three fighters return to the foreground
cards.text: The King of Fighters 2002 is Eolith's team fighting game, first released for Neo Geo on 10 October 2002 and published by Playmore. It gathers returning characters in another dream match after the NESTS storyline, bringing the series back to three-on-three battles. The selection places familiar teams from different years beside one another, with Omega Rugal returning as the final opponent. Its central changes concern the power gauge and MAX activation, giving players more ways to turn a stored resource into an immediate opportunity during an exchange.

cards.heading: Spending the power gauge
cards.text: The power gauge fills through attacks and special techniques, with later teammates able to hold more stocks. A stock can support a strong special move or a defensive answer while blocking, so spending it means choosing between immediate damage and preserving another response. MAX activation provides another option, opening a short period in which attacks can be cancelled into other moves. The system makes the order of the team relevant to resource management as well as character matchups, because each remaining fighter enters with a different potential capacity.

cards.heading: An opening becomes a combination
cards.text: During MAX activation, the player can connect actions that would otherwise end separately, creating routes into more elaborate combinations. Stronger MAX techniques ask for additional resources or low health, making their availability part of reading the round. The large returning cast gives those systems many different move sets to work with. A later remake, Unlimited Match, expanded and revised the game, but the original's appeal already rested on this direct relationship: earn power through the fight, recognise an opening and decide how much of that reserve to commit to it.
